courses.title: Welcome to Central Union
courses.description: A short orientation for newcomers: who we are as a church family, what to expect when you visit, and simple ways to get connected.

lessons.title: Who we are
lessons.body:
# A family gathered around Christ
Central Union Church of Christ is a congregation of people learning to follow Jesus together. We gather to worship, study Scripture, pray and serve our neighbors.

# What we value
- **Scripture**: we open the Bible together and let it shape how we live.
- **Worship**: we meet to praise God, share the Lord's Supper and encourage one another.
- **Community**: no one should have to walk the road of faith alone.
- **Service**: we look for ways to love our town in practical ways.

Wherever you are on your faith journey, you are welcome here.

lessons.title: What to expect on a Sunday
lessons.body:
# Arriving
Greeters at the door are happy to help you find a seat, the restrooms, or classes for children. Come as you are; there is no dress code.

# The service
A typical gathering includes singing, prayer, Scripture reading, the Lord's Supper and a sermon. Feel free to participate as you're comfortable.

# Afterward
Stick around to meet a few people. If you have questions, ask any greeter or staff member. That's what we're here for.

lessons.title: Getting connected
lessons.body:
# Find your people
The best way to feel at home is to be known. Here are a few easy next steps:
- Join a Bible class or small group.
- Take one of the classes in this app and invite a friend to take it with you.
- Sign up to serve on a team that fits your gifts.

# Stay in the loop
Make sure the church office has your contact information so you hear about events, prayer requests and opportunities to serve.

lessons.title: Your next step
lessons.body:
# Take one step this week
Growing in faith happens one step at a time. Pick **one** of these and do it this week:
- Introduce yourself to someone new on Sunday.
- Start the class **How to Read the Bible** in this app.
- Ask a leader about joining a small group.

Congratulations on finishing this orientation. We're glad you're here!

courses.title: How to Read the Bible
courses.description: A practical beginner's guide: how the Bible is organized, how to read a passage in context, and a simple method for daily reading.

lessons.title: Getting oriented: the books of the Bible
lessons.body:
# One story, many books
The Bible is a library of 66 books written over many centuries. It is divided into two main parts:
- **The Old Testament** (39 books): creation, God's covenant with Israel, the Law, history, poetry and the prophets.
- **The New Testament** (27 books): the life of Jesus in the four Gospels, the early church in Acts, letters to churches and individuals, and Revelation.

# Finding your way
References look like **John 3:16**: the book (John), the chapter (3) and the verse (16). The table of contents at the front of most Bibles is your friend.

lessons.title: Reading in context
lessons.body:
# Ask three questions
Before deciding what a verse means for you, ask:
- **What kind of writing is this?** Poetry, history, a letter and prophecy are read differently.
- **What comes before and after?** Read the whole paragraph or chapter, not just one verse.
- **Who was it written to first?** Understanding the original audience helps you understand the message.

# Let Scripture explain Scripture
When a passage is hard to understand, look for other passages that speak to the same theme.

lessons.title: A simple daily method (SOAP)
lessons.body:
# SOAP in four steps
- **S - Scripture**: read a short passage and write down a verse that stands out.
- **O - Observation**: what does it say? Note who, what, where and why.
- **A - Application**: how does this shape what I believe or do today?
- **P - Prayer**: talk to God about what you read.

# Start small
Ten to fifteen minutes a day is plenty. A good place to begin is the Gospel of Mark, one short section each day.

lessons.title: Reading together
lessons.body:
# Better together
Reading with others helps you notice things you'd miss on your own and keeps you consistent.
- Invite a friend to follow the same reading plan.
- Share one thing you learned each week.
- Bring your questions to a Bible class.

Well done! You now have the tools to read the Bible with confidence.

courses.title: Serving Well: Volunteer Basics
courses.description: Everything a new volunteer needs: why we serve, how to be a dependable teammate, welcoming guests and following safety practices.

lessons.title: Why we serve
lessons.body:
# Following Jesus' example
Jesus said he came not to be served but to serve. When we serve, we reflect his love and help the whole church family thrive.

# Every role matters
Greeting at the door, running the sound board, teaching children or preparing a meal: each role helps someone encounter God's love.

lessons.title: Being a dependable teammate
lessons.body:
# Simple habits that help
- Check your schedule and confirm when you're asked to serve.
- Arrive a few minutes early so you're ready before people arrive.
- If something comes up, let your team leader know as soon as you can and help find a replacement.
- Ask questions. No one expects you to know everything on day one.

lessons.title: Welcoming guests
lessons.body:
# First impressions last
- Smile, make eye contact and introduce yourself by name.
- Offer help without pressure: show people where to go rather than just pointing.
- Learn and use names when you can.
- Introduce newcomers to someone else so they leave with more than one connection.

lessons.title: Safety basics
lessons.body:
# Keeping everyone safe
Follow Central Union's safety policies whenever you serve. In general:
- When serving with children or youth, never be alone with a child; keep two approved adults present.
- Know where exits, first-aid supplies and fire extinguishers are located.
- Report any concern or incident to your team leader right away.

Ask your ministry leader for the specific policies and any required screening for your role.

courses.title: Prayer Practices for Everyday Life
courses.description: Grow a steady, honest prayer life with simple patterns you can use anywhere: ACTS, praying Scripture and building a daily rhythm.

lessons.title: What prayer is
lessons.body:
# Talking with God
Prayer is conversation with God. It doesn't require special words, only honesty. Jesus taught his disciples to pray simply and sincerely.

# Prayer shapes us
As we pray, we bring our needs to God, and over time prayer reshapes our hearts toward trust, gratitude and love for others.

lessons.title: The ACTS pattern
lessons.body:
# Four movements
- **A - Adoration**: praise God for who he is.
- **C - Confession**: honestly name where you've fallen short.
- **T - Thanksgiving**: thank God for specific gifts.
- **S - Supplication**: ask for what you and others need.

Try praying through ACTS for five minutes today.

lessons.title: Praying Scripture
lessons.body:
# Borrowing the Bible's words
The Psalms are a prayer book. Read a psalm slowly and turn each line into your own prayer.

Start with **Psalm 23** or **Psalm 121**. When a phrase stands out, pause and pray it back to God in your own words.

lessons.title: Building a daily rhythm
lessons.body:
# Make it a habit
- Pick a consistent time and place.
- Keep a short list of people and needs to pray for.
- Pray with others: at meals, with family or with a prayer partner.
- Be gentle with yourself on days you miss. Just begin again.

courses.title: Leading a Small Group
courses.description: Practical skills for small group leaders: planning a meeting, asking good questions and caring for the people in your group.

lessons.title: Planning a great meeting
lessons.body:
# A simple flow
- **Welcome** (10 min): food, catching up, an easy icebreaker.
- **Study** (30 min): read the passage and discuss.
- **Prayer** (15 min): share requests and pray together.

Send a reminder a day or two before, and start and end on time.

lessons.title: Asking good questions
lessons.body:
# Move from facts to life
- **Observe**: What does this passage say?
- **Interpret**: What did it mean to its first readers?
- **Apply**: What would change if we took this seriously this week?

Avoid yes-or-no questions, get comfortable with silence, and invite quieter members in by name, gently.

lessons.title: Caring for your group
lessons.body:
# Shepherding well
- Follow up when someone misses a meeting.
- Celebrate milestones: birthdays, new jobs, answered prayers.
- Share leadership: let others host, lead discussion or coordinate meals.
- Know when to involve a minister for situations beyond your group's care.

Thank you for leading. Small groups are where many people first feel truly known.
